summary: Forest Service lookout in McCormick County, SC, built May 1936 by a CCC camp; state forestry staff manned it from 1974-75; a 2020 visit found the lower stairs gone and the cab damaged.

facts.design: 100' LS-40 Aermotor tower with 7'x7' galvanized sheet metal cab with hip roof
facts.status_note: Last visit report (September 2020) says the structure looked ok but likely needs a check for structural stability; no later report found

access.note: Upper deck not open to visitors (HikingWNC); lower staircase removed and base fence mostly down (2020 Register visit report); no official closure notice found

visit.trail_note: HikingWNC lists a roadside stop of 0.1 miles round trip with no tower access

events.note: Constructed May 1936 as the fourth tower in the Long Cane Division, built by the Bradley CCC camp (Register); work reported started in May 1936 (Index-Journal item quoted by Forest Lookouts)
State Forestry Commission personnel began manning the tower in the 1974-75 season, per a state forestry report quoted by Forest Lookouts
Registered November 17, 2009 as US 838, SC 8; nominated by Ron Stafford
Visit report dated September 16, 2020: bottom staircase removed, windows broken, base fence mostly pulled down

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the Forest Service used the tower actively until the 1980s; the Forest Lookouts quote says state forestry personnel began manning it in 1974-75. The sources do not say how the work was shared, so the story reports both without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Only one visit report (September 2020) appears on the Register page, so current condition is unknown. Access is set to restricted from HikingWNC plus the 2020 report; no official closure notice was found. HikingWNC is a hiking site, not an agency. The Index-Journal text is available only as quoted by Forest Lookouts. No photos added.
